qualitative.source: claude-code subagent (viewed all 3 contact sheets + profile + transcript; YouTube offers no transcript for this video, so story is read from burned-in subtitles)
qualitative.summary: An access-driven Gambia episode in which the creator spends a week alongside a presidential candidate (a 'Talib' campaign T-shirt is visible at 0:10). Most of it is observational: car ride-alongs, security staff opening SUV doors, community clean-up activity and a long sit-down in a mayor's office. Black interstitial cards ('ZERO TO £100M', 'THE NEXT DAY') reset the chronology. Pieces to camera in a hotel corridor and an office state the stakes ('He's running for president and I'm here to support him'). The film ends on an extended in-car conversation with the candidate and closes on 'NEXT RELEASE' and 'SEE YOU NEXT TIME' black cards.
qualitative.hook_analysis: In medias res. The film opens in a dark car interior with a magenta-lit window at 0:00, cuts to campaign supporters at 0:10 and an SUV at a restaurant entrance at 0:20, and only then shows the series card at 0:30. Context comes after it, from in-car subtitles ('we just wrapped up a couple of activities'). The viewer is placed inside the entourage before being told why. A radio line in the subtitles at 1:19 ('...the presidential election is here') supplies the stakes without a presenter.
qualitative.narrative_arc: Day-by-day chronology. Day 1 (0:39-3:17) covers the car, the candidate's home and a community clean-up ('Set-settal', 2:18). 'THE NEXT DAY' (3:27) leads to a stakes-setting piece to camera at 4:07-4:46, then a hotel, a car, and a restaurant meeting (7:14-8:23). After a short wrap piece to camera (9:23-10:02), a second 'THE NEXT DAY' (10:12) leads to the mayor's office: a piece to camera with facts (10:52-11:51), then a long observational interview with the mayor (12:01-14:58). The climax is a reflective in-car conversation about leadership and risk (15:28-17:26), followed by end cards.
qualitative.camera_and_composition: Handheld observational framing. Car interiors are shot in profile against bright windows, sometimes as near-silhouettes (5:55-6:15, 15:48-17:26). There is a dashboard POV of the street (6:25), and a rear-view-mirror detail with a campaign air-freshener reading 'A NEW GAMBIA IS POSSIBLE' (15:18). Pieces to camera are eye-level medium close-ups with shallow depth of field (4:07-4:46). The mayor scene holds a static wide two-shot in which the presenter sits frame right and partly cut off (12:10-14:58). Exact cuts and camera moves are not observable at storyboard resolution.
qualitative.color_and_grade: Warm overall (mean warmth 0.09), with red/terracotta walls dominating the restaurant and office scenes (palette #633729, #953836). Car windows clip to magenta/pink (0:00, 0:39-0:59, 6:35), which looks like a deliberate or tolerated stylisation. Exteriors are saturated greens and oranges. Shadows are kept fairly dark (low-key tag on the opening scene).
qualitative.sound_and_music: Not measurable: YouTube offers no transcript and no audio was downloaded. Burned-in subtitles show continuous dialogue through most scenes, plus one on-screen caption describing radio audio at 1:19. Subtitles continue over the black 'NEXT RELEASE' card at 17:36, so dialogue audio probably runs under the end card.
what_to_borrow: Open inside the moving car or the action, and hold the title card until about 30 s in
Use plain black text interstitials ('THE NEXT DAY') to mark time jumps in a multi-day trip
Use one direct piece to camera to state the stakes, placed after the viewer has already seen the world
Let a long in-car conversation be the emotional climax instead of a montage
Use found text in the environment (campaign air-freshener, T-shirts) as story exposition
what_to_avoid_copying: 'ZERO TO £100M' series card and 'NEXT RELEASE dd/mm/yyyy' cards (creator branding)
Clipped magenta car windows, unless you want that look on purpose
Static, unvaried two-shot held for almost 3 minutes (12:10-14:58); this only works when the speaker carries it

qualitative.source: claude-code subagent (viewed all 3 contact sheets + profile + transcript; YouTube offers no transcript for this video, so story is read from burned-in subtitles)
qualitative.summary: A three-day Gambia trip hosting former Manchester United striker Louis Saha, built around a charity football match. It mixes a long warm-lit dinner conversation, seated pieces to camera from the creator, a monkey-park and craft-market leisure section, and a golden-hour match with a trophy presentation. This is the most saturated and warm-graded of the six videos (mean warmth 0.19, saturation 0.47). It closes with an airport farewell, seated reflections, and the 'ZERO TO £100M' card used as an end bookend rather than an opener.
qualitative.hook_analysis: A visual teaser montage comes before any talk: a group photo (0:00), a crowd with a flag and an overlaid countdown, '242 DAYS LEFT' (0:10), security in a crowd (0:20), and sun through leaves (0:30). Then a seated piece to camera at 0:40 explains the event and the guest. It is a short visual lead-in followed by speech, with the countdown text supplying urgency.
qualitative.narrative_arc: Arrival and setup by piece to camera (0:40-1:59). Dinner conversation on entrepreneurship versus football (2:08-7:35). Hotel-lobby reflection piece to camera (7:45-8:54). Leisure: monkey park and market (9:04-11:52). Fans and convoy (12:02-13:30). Charity match at golden hour (13:40-15:39). Trophy and speeches (15:49-16:38). Night farewell talk (16:58-17:47). Seated debrief (17:57-18:47). Louis leaving the airport (18:57-19:46). Final reflection and end cards (19:56-21:05).
qualitative.camera_and_composition: Eye-level medium close-ups for pieces to camera, with a shallow-focus canopy or hotel atrium behind (0:40-1:59, 7:54-8:54). The dinner is covered handheld from several angles with soft foreground bottles framing faces (2:18-7:35). The monkey park uses very shallow depth of field for nature details (9:53-10:23). The match is covered from low angles behind players' backs and from the stands (14:50-15:29). Exact moves and cuts are not observable at storyboard resolution.
qualitative.color_and_grade: Strongly warm: orange/amber interiors (palette #c08447, #e3ab6b), golden-hour pinks at the match and trophy lift (15:49-16:38), and saturated greens and blues in daytime pieces to camera. The night scenes (16:48-17:47) stay warm with practical lamp highlights. This is the most 'cinematic travel' palette in the set.
qualitative.sound_and_music: Not measurable: no transcript is available and no audio was downloaded. Burned-in subtitles show dialogue-driven scenes; the 0:00-0:30 montage and the match section (13:40-15:39) have no subtitles in the sampled frames, which suggests music or ambience there, but this is unverified.
what_to_borrow: An overlaid countdown or stake number in the first 10 s ('242 DAYS LEFT') to create urgency
Bookend a guest visit with arrival and airport farewell scenes
Do the seated reflection piece to camera after the event, not only before it
Use golden hour for the set-piece event and shoot from behind players and among the crowd
Use shallow-depth nature cutaways as a breather between talk-heavy sections
what_to_avoid_copying: The 'ZERO TO £100M' and 'SEE YOU NEXT TIME' series cards
Five-minute dinner table chatter with little visual change (2:18-7:35); trim it for your own pacing
Name-dropping a famous guest in the title as the main hook if you cannot deliver access

qualitative.source: claude-code subagent (viewed all 3 contact sheets + profile + transcript (auto-captions, 389 cues))
qualitative.summary: Vlog 22 of the 'Zero to £100M' series: a lifestyle-plus-business day in Dubai. It runs from a night arrival at a serviced apartment, through lunch with friends, a long kitchen conversation about fitness and nutrition, and a yacht meeting with a European businessman about deals and listing versus staying private, to a villa dinner. It is the most 'personal vlog' of the six (style mix: personal 0.43), with first-person speech from 0:12 ('welcome to downtown Dubai'). Yellow bold labels ('THE APARTMENT', '11 AM') mark place and time. It ends on the standard black 'NEXT RELEASE' and 'SEE YOU NEXT TIME' cards.
qualitative.hook_analysis: A short visual lead-in. A night skyline (0:00) leads to the creator walking down a hotel corridor and grinning into the lens (0:10-0:20), and speech starts at 0:12 as an arrival greeting. There is no cold-open claim and no series title card in the sampled opening frames. The hook is aspirational access (skyline, Burj Khalifa view) rather than stakes.
qualitative.narrative_arc: Loose, chapter-driven day-in-the-life: Arrival (0:00-1:04), Security and Lifestyle, Entrepreneurial Mentality (a lunch table with friends, 2:09-3:38), Strategic Business Focus (the 'THE APARTMENT' backlit talk, 3:57-4:37), Fitness and Nutrition (a long kitchen sit-down, 6:06-9:04), Yacht Meeting and Deals (11:03-14:11), Listing vs Private Growth, Travel and Leisure (cruise and waterside lunch, 14:20-17:38), and Culinary Experiences (villa pizza dinner, 17:48-19:07). The arc runs from leisure through business to leisure. The stakes are implicit.
qualitative.camera_and_composition: Mixed. There are backlit, near-silhouette pieces to camera against apartment windows (4:07-4:37, 9:44), a locked-off medium shot at the kitchen counter held for minutes (6:06-9:04), a phone-screen insert (9:14), and in-taxi profiles (10:03-10:33). The yacht covers both people in clean, bright medium close-ups (11:32-14:11), with drone/boat wides of the marina and wake (14:40-15:10) and macro-style wine-pour details (16:29-16:39). Exact moves are not observable at storyboard resolution.
qualitative.color_and_grade: Warm wood-and-amber interiors (palette #523015, #7f5a3f) against bright, slightly washed daylight exteriors on the yacht. Night shots are low-key. Yellow bold sans-serif text labels (3:57, 11:03) are the one graphic accent.
qualitative.sound_and_music: From auto-captions: about 82% speech coverage, 135 wpm overall, 19 [music] markers, and a longest non-speech run of 47 s. Speech-free montages are flagged around 9:31, 14:33, 15:29 and 15:55 (the yacht cruise and wake). The opening 12 s has no speech, which suggests music or ambience over the skyline. The music itself cannot be identified.
what_to_borrow: Bold place/time labels ('THE APARTMENT', '11 AM') to orient the viewer in a loose day-in-the-life
Insert a phone or app screen when the talk references data
Use speech-free cruise/wake montages to give a long talk-heavy film room to breathe
Use a backlit window silhouette for a reflective monologue
what_to_avoid_copying: 'NEXT RELEASE' and 'SEE YOU NEXT TIME' series cards
A three-minute locked-off kitchen talk about fitness tracking that only loosely ties to the episode thesis
Luxury-brand signage shots (Ritz-Carlton, Burj Al Arab) as filler

qualitative.source: claude-code subagent (viewed all 4 contact sheets + profile + transcript; YouTube offers no transcript for this video, so story is read from burned-in subtitles)
qualitative.summary: A Copenhagen episode that is almost entirely one man talking. It is structured as a sit-down interview with an off-camera questioner, in a few interior setups: a green meeting room with a screen, olive velvet curtains, and a teal wall. Topics include taking the group public ('We are no longer a small business'; 31 shareholders), a whiteboard session mapping his holdings, why he wants to build in England, and the Jim Ratcliffe/INEOS conglomerate model. Coverage of the same talk changes from wide to close to over-the-shoulder. Big white time labels ('11AM', '12PM') structure the day. There are very few exteriors, and it ends on black 'NEXT RELEASE' and 'SEE YOU NEXT TIME' cards with subtitles still running.
qualitative.hook_analysis: Three atmospheric interior details come first: a teacup on a tray (0:00), a staircase (0:05) and a chandelier (0:10). Then '11AM' in large white type with an off-camera prompt in the subtitles ('Meetings. How you feel?') at 0:15, and the creator is talking by 0:30. It is a mood-setting lead-in followed by an immediate interview. The profile counts no speech in the first 30 s because there is no transcript, but subtitles appear from 0:15.
qualitative.narrative_arc: Interview chapters: UK-CPH-UAE plans (0:20-2:00) lead to Going Public (2:04-3:57), The UK Trip and inspiration from an energy CEO's speech (3:57-5:51), the whiteboard 'Vision' (5:56-7:55), Why England, with colonial/historical ties and childhood summers (8:04-10:33), and the Jim Ratcliffe model (10:48-12:36). The film closes with an outro over the end cards. The argument escalates from the company's status to personal ambition ('by the time I'm 40'), then to a national-scale vision.
qualitative.camera_and_composition: Seated interview framing, slightly off-centre, eye-level or slightly low, with a wide lens in the first setup (0:30-1:59). Later setups are tighter medium close-ups against olive curtains (8:04-10:33). The final setup is a wide over-the-shoulder with a blurred white foreground figure (10:48-12:36). The whiteboard section uses low-key side light, silhouettes, and close inserts of the pen (6:01-7:50). Storyboard sampling here is every ~4.9 s, but exact cuts and camera moves are still not observable at this resolution.
qualitative.color_and_grade: Muted, moody interior palette: olive green curtains, teal walls and warm skin tones, with a high-contrast tag. The whiteboard scene is dark with a pink/red cast on the walls (6:26-7:55). There are almost no daylight exteriors (one building facade at 9:28).
qualitative.sound_and_music: Not measurable: YouTube offers no transcript and no audio was downloaded. Subtitles run continuously, consistent with almost wall-to-wall speech. Off-camera questions appear in the subtitles (e.g. 'but why England?' at 9:28). Subtitles continue over the black end cards (12:41-12:51).
what_to_borrow: Cover a long sit-down in several distinct setups (wide, tight, over-the-shoulder) so a 12-minute talk does not feel static
Use a whiteboard drawing session as visual exposition for abstract business structure
Use large time-of-day labels to give an interview-heavy film a day structure
Put the off-camera interviewer's questions in the subtitles to signal chapter turns
what_to_avoid_copying: 'NEXT RELEASE' and 'SEE YOU NEXT TIME' series cards
Nearly no exteriors or b-roll for 12 minutes: this only works with an established audience

qualitative.source: claude-code subagent (viewed all 4 contact sheets + profile + transcript (auto-captions, 811 cues))
qualitative.summary: Vlog 60 of the 'Zero to £100M' series, titled as 'The Reality of Buying a $10M Business in London'. Over two nights in London it moves through an airport arrival, a back-seat car conversation, a meeting with a young co-founder of an M&A simulator game, a UK investor-visa event in Parliament, an Airbnb, a kitchen piece to camera pitching his coaching community, and a live deal completion on a video call ('Fuck, we just bought a new company'). After the 'NEXT RELEASE' card, about 10 minutes of bonus screen-recorded demo of the simulator follow. It is the darkest, most low-key grade (53% low-key frames) and has the densest speech (178 wpm, 98% coverage).
qualitative.hook_analysis: A music-led cold open. A rap track (its lyrics appear in the auto-captions) plays over a dark car interior with a white stat overlay, 'VLOG 60 / CURRENT REVENUE: £9M' (0:00). City b-roll with a Rolls-Royce and a cyclist (0:10) follows, then the 'ZERO TO £100M' card (0:20). At 0:26 speech starts ('Just landed in London') with the setup: a board meeting and a deal due to close. The revenue counter frames the series' progress metric before anything else.
qualitative.narrative_arc: Setup (close the deal today) comes at 1:29. Then: a car ride and the video-game launch (1:59-4:27); meeting the co-founder (5:17-7:55); the Parliament/investor-visa event (8:05-10:04); the Airbnb and a friend (10:14-11:33); the coaching pitch in the kitchen (11:43-14:22); the simulator explained to an older guest (14:32-16:01); and the climax, a video-call completion and reaction (16:11-18:59). Outro card at 19:19, then the bonus demo (19:29-29:43). It is a clear setup-to-payoff arc, with the payoff saved for the end.
qualitative.camera_and_composition: Handheld, often low-light. Airport selfie medium close-ups (0:30-1:29). A back-seat car shot from the opposite seat with a wide lens (1:59-4:27). Over-the-table restaurant shots against a window, with a dark foreground (5:17-7:46). Landmark cutaways (Big Ben 8:05, London Eye 8:45). Chandelier/light-fixture details (10:14-10:24). A kitchen piece to camera at counter height (11:53-14:22). Silhouette against net curtains for the deal call (16:11-16:41). Screen recording fills the frame in the bonus section. Exact moves are not observable at storyboard resolution.
qualitative.color_and_grade: Very warm, dim amber tungsten interiors (palette #241710, #60390c) with deep shadows. Daytime London exteriors are cool and grey for contrast. The bonus section is a blue/purple UI screen. A small amount of letterboxing is detected (10.5%). Overall it is the most 'night-time intimate' look in the set.
qualitative.sound_and_music: From auto-captions: near-continuous speech (98% coverage, 178 wpm). Thirteen [music] markers, including a rap track with captioned lyrics over the 0:00-0:22 cold open and music under the Parliament event intro (~4:36-4:57). Laughter markers (9) and one [applause] at the deal completion (~16:41). There is strong profanity in speech. The music cannot be identified beyond the caption markers.
what_to_borrow: A running metric overlay ('CURRENT REVENUE') in the first frame to anchor a series' progress
State the episode's goal early ('we're supposed to close today') and pay it off on camera at the end
Name lower-thirds for notable people at events
Contrast cool, grey exteriors with warm tungsten interiors to separate public and private moments
Film the real reaction live after a milestone call instead of re-staging it
what_to_avoid_copying: 'ZERO TO £100M' card, 'VLOG 60 / CURRENT REVENUE' counter format and 'NEXT RELEASE' card (series branding)
The 10-minute bonus product demo appended after the outro, which is advertising
Licensed rap track and heavy profanity in the cold open
Underexposed interiors where faces fall into black (19:09)

qualitative.source: claude-code subagent (viewed all 3 contact sheets + profile + transcript; YouTube offers no transcript for this video, so story is read from burned-in subtitles)
qualitative.summary: Vlog 11 of 'Zero to £100M'. Despite the 'UK' title, the frames show Copenhagen: Danish signage ('PRESSEN', 'Book dit næste...') and a rainy grey city. The creator does a long wide-angle walk-and-talk through the streets explaining how M&A works and recapping a Gambia trip. He then sits at a table in what looks like a members' club for a long coaching-call segment ('let's talk deals'). The film ends with Christmas shopping in a luxury store. It is the coolest, most desaturated grade of the six (warmth -0.015), with a teal/cyan cast.
qualitative.hook_analysis: A direct greeting piece to camera. At 0:00 he is in a café, framed tight with a wide lens and wearing a cap, and the subtitle opens 'Hi guys, welcome to vlog 11 on the journey from zero to 100 million pounds'. A low-angle traffic-light cutaway (0:29) follows, then the series card 'ZERO TO £100M' with a quoted tagline ('I just wanna hear YES') at 0:39. This is the most YouTube-vlog-style opening of the set.
qualitative.narrative_arc: Intro (0:00-0:49). Gambia recap and M&A explainer told while walking (0:59-7:41): chapter 'Gambia Trip' covers footage of Copenhagen, so the talk and the visuals are about different places. Arrival indoors (8:21-9:00). Coaching call at the table (9:10-15:03). Members' club and Christmas shopping (15:13-16:42). End card. Low dramatic stakes; the film is driven by explanation.
qualitative.camera_and_composition: Ultra-wide handheld, often selfie-style or walking alongside. The camera is low and close, with the subject off-centre and distorted architecture behind (0:59-7:41). There are low-angle cutaways of signs and traffic lights (0:29, 7:22-7:32). The table scene is a low wide-angle shot across a table with tea props in the foreground (9:10-15:03). The shop scene is handheld among mannequins (16:12-16:42). Exact moves are not observable at storyboard resolution.
qualitative.color_and_grade: Cool, desaturated, teal-shifted grade on exteriors, with lifted blacks and a slightly filmic look (dominant #0c1b1d, #f5f0dd). Interiors are warmer with tungsten lamps but stay muted. The look is distinct from his warm Africa/Dubai episodes.
qualitative.sound_and_music: Not measurable: YouTube offers no transcript and no audio was downloaded. Subtitles appear in almost every frame, suggesting continuous walk-and-talk monologue and call dialogue.
what_to_borrow: Use walk-and-talk exposition to explain an abstract topic while moving through a city
Low-angle sign and traffic-light cutaways as punctuation in long monologues
Let a strong location-specific grade (cool, rainy northern city) define the episode's mood
A tagline under the title card that quotes the episode's key line
what_to_avoid_copying: 'ZERO TO £100M' card and 'SEE YOU NEXT TIME' series branding
A title that names a different country from the one on screen
An ultra-wide lens close to the face for minutes on end, which distorts the face
